anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

bible_refs.note: Senses trained for discernment of good and evil; solid food.
One man among a thousand — possible for εἷς ἐκ χιλίων.
One and two against a thousand / myriad — possible proverb-frame.

pass_a_gloss: And very few altogether are those having the sense-organs trained toward discernment of both good and evil and partaking of solid food, who will also be able to leave nothing of the meats until morning, as he says, perhaps one out of a thousand and two out of a myriad, of whom the blessed apostles also were.
pass_b_english: And very few indeed [are] those who have senses [trained] for the [discernment] of both good and evil and who partake of [solid] food — who will also be able [to leave] none of the meats [until] morning, as he says: perhaps one [out of] a thousand and two out of a myriad, [of whom] the blessed apostles also [were].
source_text: Ὀλίγοι δὲ παντελῶς [εἰσιν] ο[ἱ] τὰ αἰσθητήρια γεγυ[μνασ]μένα ἔχοντες πρὸς διά[κρι]σιν καλοῦ τε καὶ κακοῦ καὶ [στε]ρᾶς μεταλαμβάνοντες [τρο]φῆς, οἳ καὶ δυνήσονται [μηδ]ὲν καταλιπεῖν τῶν κρε[ῶν ἕ]ως πρωΐ, ὡς λέγει, εἴς που [ἐκ] χιλίων καὶ δύο ἐκ μυρίων, [ὧν] καὶ οἱ μ[α]κάριοι ἀπόστολοι [ὑπ]ῆρχον.
